pairs.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:115 The shim-equivalence block takes any MODULE_NOT_FOUND to mean 'standalone checkout'. In-repo, a single deleted eslint-rules/<rule>.cjs shim therefore prints SKIP and run-all exits 0, and eslint.config.mjs requires the package directly rather than the shims, so lint does not catch it either: the claim that test:rules asserts the shims and the package stay one implementation goes unchecked exactly when it breaks.

techniques.evidence: packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:116 The SKIP names one producer (a standalone checkout) while a second producer (one missing shim) yields the same output. The remaining assertions are never reached, and the run reports that as a declared skip, not as a failure.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:70 The presets are flat config for external adopters' ESLint to read, but they are only checked for shape (array, rule ids resolve). They are never loaded into ESLint/Linter, so a config ESLint would reject still passes. The rules themselves do go through the reader via RuleTester.

packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/require-source-citation.test.mjs:29 A scratch directory is created on every run and no teardown removes it: no rmSync anywhere in __tests__, which breaks the reaper rule. Minor, but a real leak.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:60 The discovered suites must equal the declared rule set, so zero or fewer suites fails the run rather than passing it.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:21 A dedicated runner for its own lane; membership is decided by location and file name, not by tags.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/run-all.mjs:29 The detached package is loaded as shipped (index.cjs), then each export's create()/meta is checked. CI runs this as test:rules.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/require-source-citation.test.mjs:233 The rule reads source text, and the tests pin that comment prose cannot satisfy its needle.
packages/eslint-plugin-civic-transparency/__tests__/require-source-citation.test.mjs:263 Census mode is tested as a separate report population: cited, declared and uncited figures are all counted.

pairs.evidence: scripts/case-loops/law/applyPassSource.test.ts:6 The test's name claims a behavioural refusal, but its body only regex-matches the text of apply-amends-regen.ts. The gate's positive-integer predicate was not lifted into an importable unit, so nothing ever runs the refusal, and the comment explains the text instrument without calling it an interim.

techniques.evidence: scripts/case-loops/law/applyPassSource.test.ts:6 The name overclaims: it says 'refuses', but only text presence is asserted. The predicate could be lifted into a reachable unit rather than settling for a source grep.

scripts/case-loops/law/summariesReadCap.test.ts:12 The needle carries the call's argument shape, which the adjacent prose comment ('KG_READ_CAP, not a literal') does not spell, and the reason lives in the asserting file.

scripts/case-loops/law/amendsCensusExtract.test.ts:3 Seeds are shaped like the population (the awkward corpus classes), not like a demo. The temp dirs in tiskText/esbirkaStream are reaped in afterAll.
scripts/case-loops/law/tiskText.test.ts:61 Retry behaviour is proved by attempt counts, with baseDelayMs: 0. No elapsed-time bound is asserted.
scripts/case-loops/law/provenanceProbe.test.ts:17 The two-sided text extraction asserts that it matched something before comparing, so a needle that stops matching fails instead of comparing nothing.
